item.title: California land trust sues to block roads across a 402-acre preserve saved from housing development
item.description: In a bid to protect the Clover Valley nature preserve, Placer Land Trust has initiated a lawsuit to block infrastructure development attempts. Established four years ago, this cherished area has faced housing pressures in the past. It comprises ancient oak forests, wetlands, and vital archaeological sites. The conservation easement was created to enforce permanent protection, and the legal proceedings will reinforce this against any existing development rights.

item.title: Edinburgh's historic Palm Houses reopen after a £23.5m restoration replaced 5,750 panes of glass
item.description: The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh's Palm Houses have undergone extensive restorations costing £23.5 million over the past five years. Researchers carefully replaced all 5,750 glass panes to ensure they withstand harsh weather conditions. Following this work, nearly 600 rare plant specimens have been replanted in the glasshouses. The restoration enables continued conservation, education, and scientific discovery efforts related to endangered flora.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas courthouse vacant since 1977 faces demolition after $120 million repair estimates
item.description: In a decisive move, Nueces County officials have voted unanimously to proceed with the demolition of the aged 1914 courthouse, which has seen a decline over the decades and thwarted multiple redevelopment attempts. Expected to last around 130 days, the demolition aims to create opportunities for future development while eliminating continuous security expenses for taxpayers. While some historical artifacts will be saved, extensive asbestos contamination complicates the safe removal process.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Entrepreneur lists Aston Martin-designed home for $19.5m
item.description: Selling for $19.5 million, David Ingram's architecturally magnificent Hudson Valley home, designed by Aston Martin, is now available. The residence includes broad living spaces and striking details, reflecting five years of enhancements since he bought it in 2020. Noteworthy features include a swimming pool and an underground automotive gallery. Now focused on his wellness endeavors, Ingram rarely visits, prompting this sale of his exquisite property.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Historic Ojai Tudor once home to composer Leo Robin sells for $4.6 million
item.description: Ojai's prestigious Estelle Clark Estate, emblematic of Tudor Revival architecture, has fetched $4.6 million after its initial listing at $6.495 million. This estate, built for the glamorous silent-film star Estelle Clark, also boasts a legacy linked to acclaimed composer Leo Robin. The appeal of historically rich and restored homes continues to thrive among buyers in the Ojai area.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Indianapolis Dam Removal Project: City dismantles Emrichsville Dam; wildlife passage restored
item.description: The city of Indianapolis is set to dismantle the Emrichsville Dam as part of an initiative to revitalize the White River's natural flow. This endeavor is designed to improve aquatic habitats and ensure the safety of river goers. Funding has been obtained from a variety of federal and state organizations to assist with this project.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Submerged Archaeological Sites Study: Researchers map two underwater Aboriginal sites; stone moved 23 km
item.description: Archaeologists collaborated with Indigenous rangers to explore submerged sites off Murujuga in Western Australia. They uncovered artefacts and evidence of past human activity before rising sea levels altered the landscape. Two key locations highlighted interactions with freshwater resources and elevated terrains. The research involved several universities and emphasized the importance of Indigenous expertise in cultural heritage.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Miami teen becomes ‘Spider-Man of Brickell’ after brave chase
item.description: Harry Cossyphas, a Miami high school senior, became a local hero after chasing a theft suspect. He witnessed a robbery and immediately pursued the man into an alley, despite being pepper-sprayed. Cossyphas managed to tackle the suspect and hold him until the police arrived. The Miami Police honored him with a hero award and acknowledged his bravery and prompt response. The suspect, Yagiz Dogan, was charged with third-degree grand theft.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Doe House Listed At $27 Million: 1908 Pacific Heights mansion hits market; bay views meet modern luxury
item.description: Built in 1908 for timber magnate Frank P. Doe, Doe House merges historic charm with modern amenities. Spanning 8,175 square feet, it boasts seven spacious bedrooms and ample outdoor spaces. Nestled in Pacific Heights, the mansion offers breathtaking views of Lafayette Park and San Francisco Bay. With its recent renovations that preserve the original Edwardsian style, this $27 million estate is a remarkable find for discerning buyers.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Historic Inn Becomes Commons: Community restores 1901 landmark; raised to cut flooding risk
item.description: The former Island Inn on Ocracoke Island has been reborn as a vibrant community and cultural hub, thanks to the passionate efforts of local residents and the Ocracoke Preservation Society. Faced with the threat of redevelopment, they successfully restored the historic building, which now hosts a variety of educational programs and community gatherings. Key renovations improved its safety and flood resilience.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian villages, torch cars and trees during olive harvest
item.description: Residents and human rights organisations say Israeli authorities have done little to stop settler attacks. They allege that soldiers have sometimes helped settlers, protected them or stood by while Palestinian villages came under assault. The violence has prompted accusations of “ethnic cleansing”, including from the British government, which accused Israel of turning a “blind eye” to the campaign.

item.title: ‘Don’t have to do this’: Trump tells new press secy Zacharia she can quit if she wants
item.description: Katie Zacharia has faced significant scrutiny after her brief tenure as White House press secretary. Donald Trump expressed concerns about the job's challenges and suggested she reconsider her position. The media has provided harsh coverage of her professional background and recent press briefing. Despite his doubts, Trump emphasized that the decision about her future is ultimately up to her.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Russia strikes 9 Ukrainian regions as new report shows spike in civilian casualties
item.description: Russia's recent strikes have plunged Ukraine into darkness, impacting electricity for hundreds of thousands and resulting in civilian injuries. Amidst this turmoil, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy voiced his worries over diminishing US support during a summit in Brussels. Civilian casualties surged by 85% in September compared to last year, as Ukraine urgently calls for more military aid while the EU seeks to enhance its support for the beleaguered nation.

item.title: Off-duty US soldier saves gunshot victim, earns Army Commendation Medal for quick first aid
item.description: When gunfire erupted near his residence, Private First Class Stephen Bradley sprang into action, showcasing his military training to help a gunshot victim. His quick thinking involved applying a tourniquet and pressure dressing, stabilizing the civilian's injuries until emergency responders arrived. Local authorities are actively investigating the shooting, while Bradley's bravery earned him the Army Commendation Medal for his commendable response during this critical situation.
